inspection_summary: Inspected all 3,103 normalized lines of Rudnick and Sarnak's article. The source develops a complete semantic chain from primitive automorphic L-functions and normalized zero statistics, through an explicit-formula conversion to prime sums and Rankin-Selberg second-moment control, to diagonal pairing and a partition-lattice/Spitzer combinatorial identification with the GUE determinant. The appendix supplies the local representation-theoretic factorization and global coefficient bounds used upstream. Prose and logical structure are recoverable throughout, while many displayed formulas have text-layer degradation and require the retained PDF for symbol-exact reuse.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Frames primitive principal L-functions as building blocks, defines normalized zero correlations, states the restricted-support GUE results, and previews the explicit-formula/diagonal/combinatorial proof mechanism.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Background on L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds local and global L-function data, functional equations, the smooth explicit formula, Rankin-Selberg analytic input, coefficient mean-square asymptotics, and Hypothesis H.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Sums over primes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transforms smoothed unrestricted zero sums into prime sums, isolates multiplicative diagonals, suppresses off-diagonals, evaluates pairings, analyzes the support barrier, and removes smoothing under RH.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Combinatorial Sieving
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses partition-lattice Möbius inversion to restore distinct indices and proves that the resulting Fourier-side distribution is the GUE determinant via marked partitions, cycles, and Spitzer's walk identity.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Appendix
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Describes Langlands-quotient local factors at finite and archimedean places, derives Rankin-Selberg coefficient positivity, and proves finite-place and archimedean parameter bounds used in the main argument.

sections_inspected.label: References and author addresses
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and end matter inspected for completeness; it contains no additional source-depth unit.

accepted_units.title: Primitive factors and the local-scale zero-statistics question
accepted_units.why_material: The article treats cuspidal GL_m L-functions as irreducible building blocks for general L-functions, then normalizes zero ordinates to unit mean spacing so that Poisson behavior can be contrasted with structured local statistics.
accepted_units.context_note: The factorization motivation, RH-based real ordering, zero-density scale, and statistical question form one necessary setup.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The normalization is displayed with degraded superscripts and spacing; the checked prose is clear, but symbol-exact reuse should consult the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: GUE level repulsion as the target local law
accepted_units.why_material: Montgomery's pair correlation and Odlyzko's computations motivate the GUE spacing law, whose quadratic vanishing at zero encodes repulsion rather than Poisson independence.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Fredholm-determinant characterization because it supplies the structural meaning of repulsion, not merely an empirical analogy.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The kernel and determinant formulas are legible in substance but require PDF verification for exact typography.

accepted_units.title: n-level correlations as translation-invariant cluster statistics
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces consecutive-spacing questions by all n-level correlation functions and explains how symmetry, diagonal-translation invariance, and rapid decay make a test function count localized clusters of normalized zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps both finite-set and smoothed-height formulations so the later analytic surrogate remains linked to the intended statistic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions are prose-recoverable; displayed normalizations and summation marks should be checked against the PDF before formal transcription.

accepted_units.title: GUE determinant density and the coefficient hypothesis
accepted_units.why_material: The sine-kernel determinant is the comparison density, while the square-summability condition on higher prime-power coefficients isolates the arithmetic assumption needed to make that universal target accessible.
accepted_units.context_note: The determinant's collision-zero behavior and the mildness of the coefficient condition jointly state the random-matrix target and analytic gate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent; prose recovers the roles, but exact determinant, kernel, and coefficient exponents need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Restricted-support GUE correlation theorems
accepted_units.why_material: Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 state the smoothed result without RH and the unsmoothed correlation result with RH, both under a Fourier-support restriction and with a universal GUE limit.
accepted_units.context_note: The two statements must remain paired: smoothing removes RH from the analytic theorem, while RH permits the direct zero statistic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Central displayed asymptotics are extraction-sensitive and require the PDF for symbol-exact use.

accepted_units.title: Support saturation, primitivity, and second-moment universality
accepted_units.why_material: The remarks separate three mechanisms: diagonal saturation at the Fourier boundary, failure of GUE for products through multiplicity or independent superposition, and universality across primitive L-functions arising from a common Rankin-Selberg second moment despite nonuniversal prime coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is a conceptual audit of what the theorem does and does not claim, including the conjecture beyond restricted support.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; a few support inequalities and product formulas should be verified in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Proof architecture from zeros to primes to determinant cycles
accepted_units.why_material: The integrated explicit formula converts zero correlations to tractable prime sums, unique factorization selects diagonal pairings, and the pairing structure is matched to cycles in the GUE determinant by combinatorial identities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the article's clearest reusable strategic blueprint and links the roles of Sections 2–4 and the appendix.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-grounded; no external reconstruction required.

accepted_units.title: Principal local factors and Ramanujan-type parameter control
accepted_units.why_material: The Euler product is organized uniformly across unramified and ramified primes through local parameters, then finite and archimedean bounds delimit the analytic region available to contour and coefficient arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the zero-parameter convention at ramified places and the distinction between conjectural tempered bounds and the weaker proven global estimate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product and exponent typography are degraded; exact local-factor formulas and bounds need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Functional equation, nontrivial zeros, and the density scale
accepted_units.why_material: Completion by the archimedean factor yields analytic continuation and a contragredient functional equation; its gamma factors determine the leading zero count and hence the normalization used in correlations.
accepted_units.context_note: The symmetry of zeros and the counting asymptotic are retained together because the latter is not an isolated normalization choice.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is reliable; constants and conjugations in displayed equations need PDF confirmation.

accepted_units.title: Smooth explicit formula as a zeros-to-prime-coefficients bridge
accepted_units.why_material: The logarithmic derivative packages prime powers into coefficients c_pi(n), and contour shifting plus the functional equation expresses a smooth sum over zeros in terms of conductor/gamma contributions and Fourier-localized prime sums.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the proof mechanism—residues, contour reflection, and Dirichlet-series evaluation—because it explains why smoothing permits the bridge.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several contour symbols are corrupt in the text layer; the semantic route is recoverable from prose, but every displayed identity needs retained-PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Rankin-Selberg convolution as second-moment access
accepted_units.why_material: The self-convolution encodes squared local coefficients, has a simple pole at one and a controlled completed functional equation, and supplies the analytic continuation and growth properties needed for Tauberian and contour arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the comparison between integral and Eisenstein-series approaches because it explains which analytic properties each method supplies.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent with line-wrap losses around half-plane inequalities; exact statements require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Universal coefficient mean square from the Rankin-Selberg pole
accepted_units.why_material: Differentiating the Rankin-Selberg logarithmic derivative and applying Tauberian/contour arguments turns its simple pole into a universal quadratic-log asymptotic for the weighted mean square of c_pi(n), with a sharpened error under Hypothesis H.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the arithmetic compression that later makes all diagonal pairings independent of the particular primitive representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The chain of Dirichlet series, residues, and weighted sums is extraction-sensitive; consult the PDF for exact weights and constants.

accepted_units.title: Verification of Hypothesis H in degrees at most three
accepted_units.why_material: Ordering the three Satake parameters, using determinant/contragredient symmetry, the global parameter bound, and Rankin-Selberg convergence controls every fixed higher prime power, proving the technical hypothesis for m <= 3.
accepted_units.context_note: The m=3 argument is the substantive case; m=2 follows by the same mechanism and m=1 is immediate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several inequalities are visually damaged; the proof strategy is prose-recoverable but exact exponents need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Unrestricted smoothed correlations as the analytic surrogate
accepted_units.why_material: The distinct-index statistic is replaced temporarily by an unrestricted sum, smoothed at height T and Fourier represented; Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 predict a measure consisting exactly of disjoint pair contributions, with distinctness deferred to a later sieve.
accepted_units.context_note: The deliberate relaxation of distinctness is essential: it makes factorization possible and creates a clean modular separation between analysis and combinatorics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The pairing-measure display is crowded and needs PDF verification, while its prose description and index structure are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Applying the explicit formula coordinatewise and localizing prime products
accepted_units.why_material: Fourier inversion lets the explicit formula act on each zero coordinate, expanding the correlation into signed prime-sum terms; compact Fourier support bounds individual prime powers and the total product below T^(2-delta).
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the gamma-term kernel bounds because they control the supposedly neutral coordinates in the product expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many displayed functions and inequalities have layout damage; exact formulas require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Multiplicative equality forced by Fourier support
accepted_units.why_material: Once neutral Fourier coordinates are truncated, the zero-sum constraint makes the logarithm of the ratio of the positive and negative prime products too small for two distinct integers of the allowed size, forcing exact diagonal equality.
accepted_units.context_note: This discrete gap argument is the decisive bridge from analytic localization to arithmetic diagonal structure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integer-gap inequalities are readable only in outline in the text layer; exact powers of T require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Truncation and off-diagonal suppression without a large sieve
accepted_units.why_material: Tail bounds for the gamma kernels, divisor-convolution estimates, dyadic decomposition, and Cauchy-Schwarz show that removing the truncated region and retaining unequal prime products contributes below the main T log T scale.
accepted_units.context_note: This realizes the introduction's claim that soft estimates suffice; the reusable idea is to combine the Fourier product bound with multiplicative-energy control.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This is the most extraction-damaged analytic span; prose identifies the reductions, but displayed bounds and equation-level reuse require the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Evaluating diagonal integrals by rescaling and Parseval
accepted_units.why_material: After exact product matching, a change to localized Fourier variables freezes the test function at logarithmic prime coordinates; Parseval and Stirling evaluate the remaining gamma-kernel integral and expose the correct T and log powers.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the uniform Taylor error and kernel integral evaluation together because both are needed to justify replacing the analytic integral by a diagonal arithmetic sum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed changes of variables and constants need PDF verification; the surrounding prose recovers the evaluation mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Only prime pairings survive at main order
accepted_units.why_material: Higher prime-power coincidences and unmatched numbers are bounded, while equal numbers with the same number of factors reduce by unique factorization to permutations of distinct primes; repeated use of the universal second moment then produces the disjoint-pair integral.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the analytic origin of Wick-like pairings and explains why detailed coefficient distributions disappear from the leading term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several multiple sums are layout-damaged; exact coefficients, domains, and constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The Fourier-support boundary is a method-sensitive saturation threshold
accepted_units.why_material: For zeta, the pole and nonnegative prime coefficients make the boundary where diagonal dominance fails visible; for higher degree, expected cancellation suggests a wider natural range than the proven 2/m range, while Dirichlet characters behave differently.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly distinguishes its proven support restriction from conjectured full universality and gives a solver-bottleneck explanation rather than treating the restriction as intrinsic truth.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Heuristic sums and exponents are extraction-sensitive; prose supports the comparison, but numerical powers require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Removing smooth cutoffs and reconciling zero normalizations
accepted_units.why_material: Under RH, approximation by admissible majorants/minorants extends the smooth limit to interval indicators, and a mean-value estimate shows that local log-gamma normalization agrees at main order with the initial unit-spacing normalization.
accepted_units.context_note: These are the two transfer steps needed to turn the analytic surrogate into the stated zero-correlation theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The approximation logic is prose-clear; displayed error estimates and normalization constants should be verified in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Partition-lattice Möbius sieve for distinct zero indices
accepted_units.why_material: Coincidence patterns of unrestricted index tuples are encoded as set partitions; embeddings identify lower-order correlations, and Möbius inversion subtracts every diagonal pattern to recover the distinct-index statistic.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a general representation change from equality constraints to incidence algebra, independent of the particular analytic input.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The partial-order glyph is degraded, but the prose and inversion equations recover the direction; scan verification is advised for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Pushing correlation measures through partition embeddings
accepted_units.why_material: Delta constraints describe the Fourier subspace induced by each partition, allowing Theorem 3.2's pairing measure to be pushed forward and Möbius-combined; the remaining goal is precisely equality with the Fourier transform of the sine-kernel determinant.
accepted_units.context_note: This span isolates Theorem 4.1 as the exact interface between arithmetic pairings and random-matrix cycles.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-heavy; exact delta products and support domain require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Reducing the GUE identification to a subset identity
accepted_units.why_material: The Möbius side factors into subset functions X_S, the determinant Fourier transform factors into cycle-overlap functions Y_S, and equality reduces to a local identity for every zero-sum subset under the support bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The reduction compresses a global determinant comparison into independent combinatorial components.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions of X_S and Y_S are visually dense and require the PDF for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Marked partitions and permutation cycles produce the two factorizations
accepted_units.why_material: Marking paired blocks makes the Möbius-side factorization explicit, while decomposing determinant permutations into disjoint cycles and applying Parseval yields the Fourier-side interval-overlap factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The two proofs expose parallel decompositions—partition reduction and cycle decomposition—that set up the final componentwise comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Some marking superscripts and products are damaged; conceptual structure is prose-grounded, but equations need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Spitzer random-walk identity closes the arithmetic-to-GUE bridge
accepted_units.why_material: Cycle overlap is reinterpreted as one minus the range of a zero-sum walk; Spitzer's unique rotation below a chord and upper-convex-envelope decomposition count that range by set partitions, proving the subset identity needed for the GUE determinant.
accepted_units.context_note: The random-walk perspective is the key semantic bridge from Fourier interval intersections to factorial subset weights.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument is well supported by prose; exact factorial sums and figure-dependent geometry should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Langlands quotients organize general local factors
accepted_units.why_material: A non-tempered generic local representation is decomposed into tempered blocks with ordered real parameters, tempered blocks into square-integrable constituents, and principal L-factors multiply along both stages.
accepted_units.context_note: This abstraction reduces all local calculations to square-integrable finite and real cases handled next.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Representation-theoretic prose is clear; product notation should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: p-adic twist classes factor the self Rankin-Selberg local term
accepted_units.why_material: Square-integrable p-adic representations are built from supercuspidals, Rankin-Selberg factors vanish outside matching twist classes, and regrouping matched blocks into explicit positive-factor products locates the first pole and bounds local Langlands parameters below one half.
accepted_units.context_note: The twist-class partition is the structural device connecting local classification to the analytic bound used in Section 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerous indices and shifts are extraction-sensitive; exact local-factor products require the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Local factorization yields nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients
accepted_units.why_material: Taking logarithms of the twist-class product writes each relevant coefficient as sums of squared magnitudes, giving a lower bound that implies nonnegativity of the global Rankin-Selberg Dirichlet coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: This positivity is later the prerequisite for Landau's theorem and thus for global parameter bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact exponents and divisibility conditions need PDF verification, though the sum-of-squares mechanism is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Archimedean factor classification and a global proof of the half-bound
accepted_units.why_material: Real Langlands quotients reduce to characters and discrete series, whose gamma factors give the completed local term; comparing the first local pole with global Rankin-Selberg holomorphy proves the archimedean parameter half-bound and avoids a more complicated local classification proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The explicit local-versus-global proof comparison is a reusable method-selection insight.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gamma shifts and tensor-product cases are formula-dependent and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Landau positivity sharpens finite-place parameter bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Nonnegative Rankin-Selberg coefficients plus meromorphic continuation let Landau's theorem bound coefficient growth; taking high powers isolates each local parameter and yields the exponent 1/2 minus 1/(m^2+1), with an analogous spherical archimedean estimate cited.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the dependency loop from the appendix back to the coefficient bounds used in Sections 2 and 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent typography is broken across lines; the bound's exact formula must be checked in the retained PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Explicit-formula-to-GUE causal chain
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Smoothing and Fourier localization turn zeros into bounded prime products; discreteness forces multiplicative diagonals, universal second moments reduce them to pairings, and Möbius/cycle combinatorics identifies those pairings with the GUE determinant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The chain is proved only under the source's coefficient and Fourier-support hypotheses, and the unsmoothed statement additionally uses RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality through a compressed second moment
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Nonuniversal prime-coefficient laws can yield universal local zero correlations because the diagonal main term retains only the Rankin-Selberg-controlled second moment and its induced pairings.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This explains the leading term in the proved restricted-support regime; it does not establish unrestricted universality or universality for nonprimitive products.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Support restriction as an analytic dominance boundary
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The Fourier cutoff controls prime-product size and diagonal dominance; the source's own heuristics show that the proven 2/m range can reflect available off-diagonal control rather than the conjectured final law.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The wider range is heuristic and depends on cancellation behavior that differs between higher-degree cusp-form coefficients and degree-one characters.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Primitivity prevents superposed zero processes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Primitivity is structurally aligned with a single GUE-type process: products create repeated or independently superposed zero sets, whereas a primitive factor's diagonal main term is internally paired through its own coefficients.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The superposition discussion is a natural conjectural interpretation, not a complete classification theorem for every nonprimitive L-function.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local-global feedback loop for analytic control
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Local representation structure makes Rankin-Selberg coefficients positive and locates local poles, while global continuation, holomorphy, and Landau estimates feed back to sharpen local parameter bounds used in the global prime-sum analysis.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several exact local formulas are text-layer fragile, and the strongest archimedean improvement stated at the end is cited for the spherical case rather than derived there.
